suggestions.rationale: Systematic-review evidence reports a substantially increased long-term frequency of knee osteoarthritis after ACL injury. Individual review should confirm that osteoarthritis is documented in the injured knee and should consider associated meniscal or cartilage injury, recurrent instability, treatment history, alignment, age, activity, and other osteoarthritis risk factors rather than inferring an individual relationship from population data alone.
evidenceGaps: Records establishing the ACL injury and affected knee
Longitudinal knee imaging and orthopedic records documenting osteoarthritis after the injury
Meniscal or cartilage injury, instability, treatment, reinjury, alignment, and other osteoarthritis risk-factor history
Orthopedic assessment addressing the individual's chronology and competing explanations

sourceReferences.citation: Webster and Hewett, Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury and Knee Osteoarthritis: An Umbrella Systematic Review and Meta-analysis, Clin J Sport Med. 2022;32:145-152. PMID 33852440
sourceReferences.note: Umbrella systematic review/meta-analysis reporting markedly increased odds of knee osteoarthritis after ACL injury; supports focused post-traumatic research, not an automatic individual conclusion.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 33852440; abstract; 13 reviews and summary meta-analysis of knee osteoarthritis after ACL injury
